measures: the packaged Windows build: disk footprint, cold start, and whether it names any external host
note: The fetch count is a static read of every template, stylesheet, script and SVG the build serves to a browser, looking only where a request is actually caused: an element's src, a stylesheet link, a CSS url() or @import, a fetch call, and a form's action. An earlier version of this check counted any address anywhere in a file and reported 36 outside hosts, every one of them a bug tracker in a comment, a line of licence text, or the w3.org namespace that every SVG declares and nothing requests. Hosts behind an anchor are counted separately, because a link a person has to click is not something the page loads. The bundled third-party packages are not scanned; they are not served. This is a reading of the files rather than a capture of the traffic, so it is evidence and not proof: it would not catch an address assembled at runtime. Cold start is wall-clock from launching the executable to the port answering, which covers unpacking, Django startup and the migration check, but not the first prediction.
